block.prompt:
Finally, the phone lines. Two callers, two very different views. Listen twice, then complete the task.

[Your teacher reads:]
Caller 1 (Priya): “I understand that people are frustrated, but tourism is not the enemy. It has lifted whole regions out of poverty. The answer is better management, not blaming visitors. If we turn people away, we lose the money that keeps these communities alive — and we send a message that some places are only for the rich who can afford to stay a week.”
Caller 2 (Tomás): “With respect, that's the argument we've heard for twenty years, and the situation has only got worse. At some point ‚better management' becomes an excuse for doing nothing. When local families are driven out and the streets are impassable, the town has already lost the thing that made it special. Sometimes the only real solution is a hard limit on numbers, even if it costs money.”

(a) Sum up each caller's main position in ONE sentence of your own.
(b) Whose argument do you personally find more convincing, and why? You must refer to at least one specific point that EACH caller made.
block.answer_key: (a) Priya: tourism brings prosperity and should be managed better, not cut — turning visitors away would harm communities and make places elitist. Tomás: “better management” has failed for twenty years and become an excuse; once residents are pushed out the town has already lost its character, so sometimes a hard cap on numbers is the only real solution. (b) Open. A strong answer states a clear preference AND engages with a specific point from each caller (e.g. agreeing with Priya's ‚only for the rich' worry, but conceding Tomás's point that twenty years of ‚management' have not worked). Reward genuine weighing of both sides over a one-sided opinion.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Beide Positionen sind vertretbar; bewertet wird die Qualität der Abwägung und der konkrete Bezug auf JE einen Punkt beider Anrufer:innen, nicht die gewählte Seite.

levels: Both positions summed up accurately in the student's own words
One position clear, the other vague or partly wrong
Clear stance that engages with a specific point from EACH caller
Stance stated but only one caller's point used
Opinion asserted with no reference to what was heard
Ideas connected with a good range of language; errors minor
Adequate range; some errors but meaning stays clear

watch_outs: Häufigster Fehler bei (b): eigene Meinung ohne Rückbezug auf das Gehörte (‚I think too many tourists is bad'). Auf den geforderten Bezug zu JE einem konkreten Punkt bestehen.
Bei (a) neigen Schüler:innen dazu, wörtlich mitzuschreiben statt in EINEM eigenen Satz zusammenzufassen — Paraphrase einfordern.
Tomás' ‚that's the argument we've heard for twenty years' ist ironisch-kritisch gemeint — die abtuende Haltung sollte erkannt werden, nicht als neutrale Info.
